subject: Retention granularity & customer-held logs: workflow and attestation
messages:
From: Julia Nguyen <julia.nguyen@acmepharm.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, security@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on log retention granularity and customer-held logs

Hi Marissa —

We're working through the SIG and CAIQ answers for our procurement review and have two related asks about Redwood's log retention model that came up from our legal/compliance team:

1) Retention granularity: can you confirm whether retention is applied at the customer-tenant level only, or if we can request finer-grained rules (per-project or per-model)? Our internal policy sometimes requires different TTLs for production vs. staging environments.

2) Customer-held logs: for certain regulated workflows we need to be able to request a short-term hold (30–90 days) on raw inference logs (request metadata + prompts, not model weights). Is there an established workflow and attestation Redwood provides when a customer requests a hold? Specifically:
   - what data fields can be preserved on hold (full payload vs. redacted PII)
   - whether Redwood can provide a signed attestation and a delivery/export of preserved logs (S3 link or secure transfer)

Can you share what evidence we can provide in the SIG/SOC 2 annex to support claims about per-tenant retention controls and a customer hold process?

Appreciate a quick note so we can keep the procurement timeline moving.

Thanks,
Julia
Julia Nguyen
Senior Information Security Manager
AcmePharm, Inc.

---
Note: attachment referenced by Acme: "acme-questionnaire-excerpt.pdf" (type: pdf, 120KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Nguyen <julia.nguyen@acmepharm.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on log retention granularity and customer-held logs

Hi Julia —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front:
- Retention is configurable at the tenant level today; we do support scoped exceptions per-environment via a customer config (we can document steps).
- We support customer-requested holds for request-level logs (metadata + prompt text) via a defined preservation workflow. We can provide an attestation and an export bundle (S3/secure link) on request; PII redaction options are available as part of the request intake.

I'll coordinate evidence for the SIG/SOC2 annex. For the intake we typically need:
1) Written customer request (email) with scope and retention period
2) Legal approval (customer) if data contains regulated PHI/PII
3) Our internal change ticket (JIRA-OPS-1147) and a short attestation doc we sign

What I'll send next: a redlined copy of our retention policy sections, a sample audit_log export (CSV with masked identifiers), and a draft DocuSign attestation template.

Are you okay with a 72-hour SLA for delivery of an export once the request is approved by both sides? If Acme needs faster turnaround we can discuss escalation/deal terms.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0127

Attachments: redwood-retention-policy-v1.2.pdf (policy extract)

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: internal - question on retention granularity & holds (Acme)

Marissa / Stephanie —

Quick notes from Legal/Ops side:
- We can attest to the tenant-level TTL config and exceptions, but per-project TTLs require an ops ticket and customer-signed request. We'll document the exact fields we persist and how we redact.
- For the attestation template: include: scope (data categories), retention window, export mechanism, chain-of-custody statement, and who signs on Redwood's side (me as Legal Ops + one engineering lead).
- SLA: 72 hours post-approval is reasonable for standard exports if data volume < 250GB. Anything larger triggers a scoped delivery (S3 presigned link + transfer plan).
- Cost: we typically treat ad-hoc preserves/exports as a billable professional-services item unless covered by the contract. Flag to sales.

I'll prepare a short Legal Ops memo and the attestation text. Stephanie, can you confirm operational steps and the JIRA ticket template?

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Nguyen <julia.nguyen@acmepharm.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 15:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question on log retention granularity and customer-held logs

Hi Julia —

Thanks for the question and apologies for the short delay. We've reviewed scope with Legal and Engineering and can confirm the following workflow we propose for AcmePharm:

1) Intake: Customer sends a signed request (email to security@redwood.ai and your account rep). We capture scope: tenant(s), environment(s), data categories (request metadata, prompts, response text), retention window to preserve, and whether PII redaction is required.

2) Approval: Redwood Legal (Rishi) confirms legal posture and Sales confirms billing terms for preservation/export (if applicable).

3) Execution: Engineering creates a preservation JIRA (JIRA-OPS-1147) and snapshots the relevant request logs. We store the preserved set in encrypted S3 with restricted ACL for the requested retention window. Sample export includes audit_log_sample.csv (masked ids).

4) Attestation & Delivery: Once export is ready we generate a DocuSign attestation (template attached) that covers chain-of-custody, fields preserved, retention end-date, and delivery mechanism. Delivery options: presigned S3, secure FTP, or PGP-encrypted archive.

We can meet the 72-hour SLA for preserves <250GB after approvals. Larger requests will include a scoped delivery schedule and an estimated delivery date.

Deliverables I'm attaching now: redwood-retention-policy-v1.2.pdf (relevant excerpts), audit_log_sample.csv (sample with masked identifiers), and docsign-customer-hold-template.pdf (DocuSign-ready attestation).

Next steps: if this workflow looks acceptable, reply to this thread with the scope fields filled in and we'll issue a JIRA and a DocuSign envelope for your signature.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Customer Success Manager, Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
